findings.title: The audit-drift capability label still describes the first draft: 'one sentence in (b) for the ended mark; two scenarios'
findings.recommendation: After the fresh iter-2 walk (W3) the delta's (b) clause is rewritten for BOTH marks — pointing at the engine's table and enumerating no observations — and the block carries THREE added scenarios (ended contradicted by live work; ratified mark with only a concluded exploration; ended mark on a premised stage), as specs/orbit-audit-drift/spec.md:8-12 and :28-41 read. proposal.md:85-86 still says 'one sentence in (b) for the ended mark, by pointer; two scenarios', and design.md:123's record row says 'ONE sentence in Architecture staleness check'. Relabel both to what shipped: '(b) rewritten to point at the composition table for both marks; three scenarios'. The 'one sentence the charter permits' phrasing at proposal.md:69 can stay — (b) is still one clause — but the scenario count is a plain disagreement.

findings.title: 'a bad date' no longer names a near-miss: the declared lexical limit makes a well-shaped impossible date PARSE
findings.recommendation: Since 6A, `Complete: [~] 2026-99-99 (Sal)` parses as ended (specs/orbit-architecture-engine/spec.md:12-14 and the scenario 'The lexical limit is shared and declared'). The near-miss is a MALFORMED date (`soon`), which is the word the delta uses at line 12. Change proposal.md:32 'a bad date' to 'a malformed date' so the proposal's near-miss list matches the spec's and does not read as if calendar validity were checked.

findings.title: The ended mark's inconsistency detail is specified only as 'naming the live citer' — the string's shape is left to the implementer
findings.recommendation: Task 2.2 says the `[~]` column's INCONSISTENT cells carry 'a detail naming the live citer', and task 2.4 pins that 'on an active change the detail names the change'. The existing `[x]` detail (src/core/architecture/state.ts, compose()) names the OBSERVED STATE, not a citer, so this is a new shape compose() must build from `citing`. Two implementers would converge on the observable the test pins, so this is polish: state the form once in task 2.2 — e.g. `Complete: mark is ended but <kind>:<name> is live — the mark is not honored` — so the render, the test and the audit-drift finding text read the same words.

commentary: This is the in-context confirm over two walks' additions, read against artifacts every one of which was edited since the last pass. Probed hardest: the two walks' ripples — whether each ratified direction (3A, 6A, 1B, 2A) landed in EVERY artifact that states it, since the walks edited five files by scripted replacement and one script failed its last anchor before being re-run. They did: the architect delta's unprompted route now carries both declines with a scenario each; the audit delta's (b) points at the table for both marks; the engine delta's format SHALL declares the shared lexical limit with an executing scenario; the design records every amendment against its decision. What was found is the residue that pattern predicts: the proposal's capability LABEL for audit-drift still describes the draft the walks replaced, and one near-miss word ('bad date') was made ambiguous by 6A's own declaration. Baseline survival checked by title: all five state scenarios, all four audit scenarios, and the format block's eight are present in the deltas; `ls specs/` shows no orbit-orientation directory; zero @review markers. Not verified by execution: the composition table itself — the fresh pass walked all fifteen cells against compose()/observe() and I did not repeat that walk, so this pass vouches for the ARTIFACTS agreeing with each other and with the ratified directions, not for the table a second time. The one place two implementers could still diverge is the ended-mark inconsistency detail's wording, pinned only by what the test asserts.
